months_used: flat from spring to autumn, jumps in winter
identity: Galloping and among the fairest tracks in Britain
Undulating; used for races such as the Lockinge
Starts in a chute, one turn after about 3f, then a 5f straight
layout: A wide, galloping, left-handed course with an undulating straight mile; the home straight runs almost exactly east to west.
Races from nine to thirteen furlongs start on the back straight; the round mile starts in a chute and makes one turn into a five-furlong straight.
tactics: Suits big, long-striding horses, especially when rain makes it testing.
Many winners come down the middle of the straight course; the stands' rail can be favoured depending on field size and stall position.
Only the round mile start is notably draw-sensitive.
ground: Soft ground makes Newbury a stiff test that suits long-striding stayers.
